copyPanel.formula: Area = (Number of Sides) × (Area of One Triangle)
steps: 1. Decompose the regular polygon from center into n congruent triangles
2. Find the area of one triangle using A = ½ × side × apothem (height)
3. Multiply by the total number of sides

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.

choiceFeedback: Use the right formula for each.
hints: Two stages hide here: first one triangle (base 4 cm, height 3.5 cm), then all 6 of them.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).

level3.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon both have triangles with the same base (6 ft) and the same height (5 ft). Which polygon has the greater total area? Explain why the number of sides matters.
level3.sentenceFrame: One triangle's area is ½ × ___ × ___ = ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The ___ has more area because ___.
level3.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Both polygons use identical triangles (base 6 ft, height 5 ft) — only the NUMBER of triangles differs.
Find one triangle's area with ½ × 6 × 5, then multiply by 6 for the hexagon and by 5 for the pentagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5 for one triangle. Then compare 6 copies with 5 copies and explain why the counts matter.
level3.explanation: One triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft in both polygons, so the only difference is how many copies each shape holds: the hexagon has 6 for 90 sq ft and the pentagon has 5 for 75 sq ft. The hexagon has the greater area because the number of sides is exactly the number of identical triangles you get to add.
level3.explanationEs: Un triángulo mide ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados en los dos polígonos, así que la única diferencia es cuántas copias tiene cada figura: el hexágono tiene 6 para 90 pies cuadrados y el pentágono tiene 5 para 75. El hexágono tiene mayor área porque el número de lados es exactamente la cantidad de triángulos iguales que puedes sumar.
level3.promptEs: Un hexágono regular y un pentágono regular tienen triángulos con la misma base (6 pies) y la misma altura (5 pies). ¿Cuál polígono tiene mayor área total? Explica por qué importa la cantidad de lados.
hintsEs: Ambos polígonos usan triángulos idénticos (base 6 pies, altura 5 pies): solo cambia el NÚMERO de triángulos.
Halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × 6 × 5 y luego multiplica por 6 para el hexágono y por 5 para el pentágono.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5 para un triángulo. Luego compara 6 copias con 5 copias y explica por qué importa la cantidad.
